h.strategy: Before proposing, briefly model the system: which components carry most of the signal, which are redundant, and where saturation, bottlenecks or substitution between components could occur. Then propose hypotheses that each test a DIFFERENT mechanism (e.g., redundancy, saturation/diminishing returns, bottleneck, interference, compensation, sign reversal). Prefer interactions where the intuitive answer is plausibly wrong, including cases where a usually helpful edit should help LESS or even hurt. Use varied edit fields, condition fields and both directions; no two hypotheses may share the same edit-condition pair or the same underlying reason. Each 'why' must name a concrete mechanism and what pattern would falsify it, not just say a component 'matters more'.

hyps.why: Replacing an existing skip on the direct edge gains less than adding a conv to an empty edge.
Replacing a skip that already provides connectivity gains less than filling an empty edge.
Without edge 4, edge 0 reaches the output only via the longer 1→2→3 route so its conv matters less.
A conv on the direct edge already supplies capacity, so extra depth on edge 2 has diminishing returns.
Without the direct edge the output depends more on edge 5, so a stronger op there matters more.
With the direct edge missing, cutting edge 0 removes input from most remaining paths.
With edge 0 already removed, edge 3 is a main input route so removing it hurts more.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to 1x1 loses receptive field, while the same edit over other ops is an upgrade.
Replacing the bottleneck conv with pooling loses far more than pooling over a skip or none.
Replacing the first feature-extracting conv with pooling is costlier than replacing weaker ops.
